user_scenario: You are Thaddeus Okonkwo-Lindqvist, 41, a seasonal interpretive ranger whose federal summer tour at the national lakeshore ended at the end of August; on weekends you also work a few hours at a hardware store in town. You filed your federal unemployment claim online on September 1. You are calling on a Tuesday afternoon, friendly and a bit rushed, using short sentences. You open by saying you have not received any unemployment payment yet and you would like to get paid for last week, the week ending 2026-09-12 (the Labor Day week). That is all you ask for. When the agent asks who you are, you give your name and your phone number 6085551562; when asked for more, you give the last four of your Social Security number, 1739, and your date of birth, 1985-07-09. If asked, your email is thaddeus.okonkwolindqvist@lakelandmail.net and your ZIP code is 53716. You do not know your weekly amount, balance or any figures and ask the agent to look them up. If the agent asks about your first week, you say you certified it online on September 6 and worked 17 hours at the hardware store that week. Only if the agent asks about your family do you say that your younger daughter now lives with her mother, who claims her on her own unemployment claim, and that a child support order for her came in the mail last week but has not started yet. Only if the agent asks about appeals do you say you appealed your monetary determination because wages from your second federal job were missing and that your hearing is set for September 29. Only if the agent asks about any overpayment do you say you had an overpayment in May because you misreported some earnings on your old claim, and that you paid it back in full at the end of May. When the agent explains that you need to certify the week ending 2026-09-12 yourself, you agree, and once the agent hands you the phone-line certification step you carry it out yourself with these answers: you were able and available all week, you refused no work, you worked 7.0 hours on Saturday and earned 112.00 gross, you made 0 work-search contacts because the office told you your search is waived for your first eight weeks since you have a recall date, and your employer paid you holiday pay for Labor Day, but your pay stub is not out yet so you do not know the dollar amount and you enter exactly the holiday pay amount and the timeliness choice the agent tells you to enter. If the agent asks whether it may record what it needs on your claim, you say yes, go ahead. Your payments should keep going to the checking account on file, and you say so if asked. You never suggest steps, rules or numbers yourself and you do not correct the agent. Once the agent tells you the payment for that week has been issued, you thank them and end the call.
